newsitem.title: FRANCE: Car bomb brings death back to Algiers city.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb brings death back to Algiers city.

text.p: A car bomb killed eight people and wounded 25 when it exploded outside a restaurant in El Biar, on the heights of Algiers, Algerian newspapers said on Thursday.
The blast ended a two-week lull in reported serious attacks and bloodshed in the city of an estimated four million people.

Boys selling cigarettes, women heading home, customers in the restaurant and occupants of passing cars were hit by the explosion which coincided with an attack on a police patrol in another area, Le Matin newspaper said.
The last big bomb in Algiers hit a market on July 14, killing at least 21 people and wounding about 40. Since then the violence has focused outside the capital.

In the past week, 170 people were slaughtered in villages and isolated communities in rebel attacks that Algerian papers said were revenge for 300 rebel deaths in a military offensive against a mountain hideout earlier in July.
Wednesday night's blast ripped along pavements thronged with people escaping their often overcrowded appartments in the popular working class district or simply out for the evening.
Algerian security forces, who blamed Moslem fundamentalists for the blast, gave an initial toll of three dead and 25 wounded, just after the bomb exploded at 7.40 p.m.(1840 GMT) on Wednesday.
Many of the wounded were in a serious condition.

"At the (hospital) emergency department were a dozen wounded who miraculously escaped death. Some were in a serious state and going to have surgery, including amputation of arms and/or legs," said Liberte newspaper.
From l'Universal restaurant on Boulevard Bougara, windows were shattered for a distance of some 400 yards (metres). The carcases of three burnt-out cars lay nearby.
The occupants of a passing Renault were caught with its full force, said El Watan newspaper. They were in a serious state.
One woman, whose balcony overlooked the scene, was crying out for her mother who had vanished.
A youth demanded of people on the spot: "Have you seen Moh (Mohamed), the redhead. I saw him a minute ago standing by the door to the bar."
The bomb exploded nearly three hours after a policeman and a civilian were killed and two police wounded, in an attack in La Glaciere area against a mobile patrol, Le Matin newspaper said.
It said two "terrorists" armed with Kalashnikovs had been seen in the same district three days earlier.

The return of violence to the capital, where tough measures had been announced to try to thwart car bombs, such as no parking on busy roads -- including Boulevard Bougara before 7 p.m. -- coincided with President Liamine Zeroual swearing in a team to oversee local elections planned for October.
Zeroual on Wednesday promised free and fair local elections would be held to cement democracy and bring back stability.

"I'm convinced that the Algerian people, who are putting much hope on the elections, will once again live up to this event which will help bring the definitive rupture with the situation of instability," he said.

About 60,000 people have been killed since early 1992 when authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. A fresh general election was held last June 5, with no letup in violence.
Zeroual did not mention the massacres of the past week.
Le Matin on Thursday said the latest violence in the North African country of 29 million people showed one thing: "The beast is wounded. And it can go still further in its murderous folly."
